description: Negative-benchmark fixture: Restate SDK multi-segment chain class. Tests PR #149's multi-segment chain resolver against external Context chains (ctx.run, ctx.invocation().target().send()). Internal Workflow + Invocation types have methods with the same bare names — the resolver must not bind chain segments to them.

Phase 3c records the raw external type name; Tier 2 now drops the binding.
Regression-prevention. ctx.invocation().target() multi-segment chain — .target is external.

Regression-prevention (FIXED by Phase 3c). Same multi-segment chain target. Phase 3c's external-receiver passthrough handles all three chain phantoms (Workflow.run, Invocation.target, Invocation.send) via the same mechanism — `ctx` parameter type is recorded raw, Tier 2 drops bindings.

notes:
Project name: `c-Users-user-Documents-GitHub-code-graph-bench-accuracy-synthetic-rust-restate-chain-negative`. Tests PR #149's multi-segment chain resolver: ctx.invocation().target().send() walks 3 chain segments through external builder types. Each segment's bare name (.target, .send) collides with internal Invocation methods.

EMPIRICAL FINDINGS (2026-05-02):
  1. ACTIVE PHANTOMS (3): `entry → Workflow.run`, `entry → Invocation.target`, `entry → Invocation.send`. The chain resolver binds external chain segments to internal methods via cross-package-heuristic.
  2. The forbidden pattern `entry → Workflow.target` does NOT fire because `Workflow.target` is conflated with `Invocation.target` (same bare-name; resolver picks Invocation). This is the same conflation pattern as the Diesel fixture's controls() finding.
  3. POSITIVE-CONTROL CONFLATION: `controls()` calls `w.target()` (where w: Workflow) but the edge emits as `controls → Invocation.target` (NOT `controls → Workflow.target`). Bare-name resolution again picks one of two same-named candidates. The expected_internal_calls list reflects this empirical truth — `controls → Workflow.target` is NOT in the expected list because it doesn't emit today.
